# Built-in Mount Collision Protection and Recovery

Dimension 3: what mounts and control software already do about collisions,
how that protection fails, and what recovery after a hard power cut
involves. Sources: [citations](../citations.md).

## Load- or current-based detection (the "resistance detection" alternative)

| Product | Mechanism | Coverage | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZWO AM5 | "stall detection mechanism" (staff, 2023-04) | **Only at 1440x slew speed**: "the stall protection will enable when the speed is R9(1440x), becasue it will not detect is in slow speed". Staff confirmed there is none at sidereal tracking speed. | [22] |
| ZWO AM5 (user) | "There is a current limit sensor on the mount but for some reason it didn't work... the mount actually slipped the belt" | One user report, 2022 | [14] |
| Rainbow RST-135 | Monitors "motor load, encoder error, and motor / board temperature in real time to cut off the power and warn" | Manufacturer statement; threshold not given | [37] |
| Rainbow (user) | Beeped when rammed into tripod | User report | [14] |
| Paramount Series 6 (worm) | "motors are current limited... running into a fixed object will automatically stop slewing and tracking" | Manufacturer statement | [42] |
| Pegasus NYX-101 | No current/stall detection described; high-torque warning | — | [36] |
| ZWO AM5 (teardown) | Stall detection mentioned only as the teardown author's guess about the stepper drivers, not as a collision feature | Single-user teardown | [88] |
| Sky-Watcher HEQ5 Pro (worm) | On a tripod strike the mount "repeatedly stopped, started, stopped", which the user read as a current-limit safeguard | User perception | [87] |
| Celestron AVX (worm, has slip clutch) | "no torque limiter, current detector, or anything of the sort" | User statement | [12] |

The overnight tracking crashes in [22], [13] and [6] happened at sidereal
speed. That is the speed at which ZWO staff say AM5 stall detection is not
active [22].

## Position-based limits

| Layer | Example | Known gap | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mount firmware | NYX-101 horizon/overhead/meridian limits stop both motors | Only as good as the time/position the mount holds | [36] |
| Mount firmware | iOptron meridian "Set Position Limit" 0–15°; RA mechanical stopper | Stopper can be damaged by "the large torque" if site/time or zero position is wrong, or by a manual slew past 20° | [32], [33] |
| Mount firmware | AM5 stops tracking at meridian (ZWO reply relayed by a user); AM3 turns off tracking at meridian flip limits | No user-set limits in the AM5 ASCOM driver as of 2023-01 | [51], [52] |
| PC driver | EQASCOM limits | Not applied to manual slews; need park/unpark for valid encoder positions | [46] |
| PC driver | INDI EQMod (2018) | Manual nudge "will not stop slewing even if it passes the meridian" | [47] |
| Imaging app | NINA meridian flip | One user believes there is no general travel limit; collisions short of the meridian are uncovered | [18], [48] |
| Firmware / imaging app | AM5 firmware 1.1.2 and ASIAIR | LST off by 1 h after DST. ZWO said firmware 1.3.0 fixed it (2023). A 2024 post recalls the same past problem and says "I think they fixed that" | [26], [53] |
| Imaging app | ASIAIR | Stalled after failed solve; overwrote SynScan limits | [25] |
| Controller | Gemini-2 safety limits | Depend on correct counterweight-down start position | [49] |
| Software watchdog | ADG MountWatcher | Requires ASCOM link; hardware relay option for comms loss | [4] |

## Documented failure modes of software and firmware protection

1. PC reboot removes the driver and its limits, and the mount keeps
   tracking [15].
2. Lost computer control: the mount drove into the pier "for hours" [12].
3. Wrong PC clock makes time-based limits useless [6].
4. DST/LST bugs in mount firmware and the imaging controller [26], [53].
5. Manual or hand-controller moves bypass software limits [10], [46], [47].
6. Wrong zero or home position at start-up [32], [49].
7. Collisions inside the allowed meridian window (tripod legs, piers) [18], [19].
8. Stall detection off at tracking speed (AM5) [22].

## Recovery after a hard power cut (the re-enable step)

| Mount / standard | What restart needs | Source |
|---|---|---|
| ZWO AM5/AM5N | No absolute encoders; "start from home position again" (forum). Teardown: IR home sensors on both axes | [40], [88] |
| ZWO AM5 manual (OCR) | Home sensor listed as a mechanical zero-position sensor. The teardown [88] describes infrared beam-interruption home sensors; the two are not reconciled. Return home before power-down; if not at home at start-up, home before any GoTo, or GoTo may cause damage (paraphrase) | [91] |
| ZWO AM5 | ZWO staff: an inadequate supply "seems" to cause a reboot; recommends "12V 3A power for AM5 itself" | [27] |
| iOptron HAE | Power-down memory: resume after "Select and Slew" | [34] |
| iOptron HEM27 | Power-down memory in the ManualsLib copy only; absent from the iOptron-hosted manual | [84], [32] |
| Pegasus NYX-101 | FRAM restores position; RA brake held until tracking enabled | [36] |
| Paramount (worm) | Incremental encoders need homing, else "lost in space" | [42] |
| 10Micron (worm) | Absolute encoders on both axes | [43] |
| Astro-Physics | "If the mount is not parked before power down, it may begin tracking when next powered up" | [44] |
| ASCOM standard | A mount may "require power cycling before being unparked" | [45] |
| Generic incremental encoder | Power interruption "erases the position count. Recovery forces a homing routine" | [50] |

**Requirement implication (inference).** On restore, an Astro-Physics mount
that was not parked can start tracking by itself [44]. On a mount like that,
re-powering a tripped mount could drive straight back into the obstacle.
Re-enable has to happen with tracking disabled, or after the payload has
been moved clear.

## Gaps and Limitations

- ZWO announced AM5 firmware V1.2.9 alongside the stall-detection statement
  [22]. Whether later firmware extended stall detection below 1440x is not
  documented in the sources read.
- RST-135 overload thresholds and recovery steps were not reachable (the
  supplementary manual is behind a login).
- No source states which strain wave mounts auto-resume tracking on
  power-up. Only Astro-Physics (worm drive) documents it.
- Whether iOptron power-down memory still exists in current HEM27/HAEc
  firmware is unconfirmed. The HAEc manual has no such text [35].
